standard_prerequisites.name: Integral symmetric bilinear forms on lattices and their duals
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a finite free module over the integers carrying an integral symmetric bilinear form the dual of a submodule is the set of vectors of the rational span pairing integrally with it, written with a sharp superscript. The form is called unimodular when the module equals its own dual, and nondegeneracy on a summand follows from positive definiteness of the form; the author's own notation for the dual and for the form is retained inside the counted span.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted lemma is the technical heart of the surrounding block of the chapter: it compares the quotient of a lattice by an orthogonal direct sum with the two torsion quotients attached to a submodule and its orthogonal complement.

core_obligations: Decompose the rational span: because the form is positive definite it stays nondegenerate on the submodule, so the rational span of the whole lattice is the direct sum of the rational spans of the submodule and of its orthogonal complement, and the projection onto the complement can be written down (source lines 442-444).

Show the projection lands integrally: for an element of the lattice the projection pairs integrally with every element of the complement because the form itself is integral, so the projection is a map into the dual of the complement (source lines 445-446).

Write down the resulting four-term exact sequence with the projection as its middle map and identify its cokernel, then observe that this cokernel is a quotient of the dual of the whole lattice modulo the lattice itself, using that the dual map of the inclusion of the complement splits as a map of modules over the integers (source lines 447-453).

Divide the four-term sequence by the direct sum of the submodule and its complement to obtain a short exact sequence exhibiting the wanted injection into the dual of the complement modulo the complement, and read off that the cokernels are quotients as claimed (source lines 454-459).

proof_roadmap.step: Orthogonal decomposition of the rational span and definition of the projection onto the complement.
Integrality of the projection onto the dual of the complement.
Exact sequence with the projection and identification of its cokernel as a quotient of the dual quotient.
Divide by the orthogonal direct sum and conclude the two injective maps.
